newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX ends firm, has 3,000 in its sights.
newsitem.headline: German DAX ends firm, has 3,000 in its sights.

text.p: German shares climbed further into record territory on Monday following Wall Street's higher end-of-week close and backed by a firm dollar and German debt market.
The DAX-30 index of leading German shares ended floor trade up 21.56 points or 0.73 percent at 2,954.95 after touching an all-time high of 2,961.25 earlier in the session.
Dealers said that, assuming there were no major upsets in the interest rate outlook, further gains could be expected. "I think the market will look to test 3,000 points this week," one trader said.

The first likely test of such market optimism are the U.S. consumer price data due to be released on Tuesday, traders said, noting the clear signals such information gave about the inflationary outlook in the U.S.
Among individual shares, DAX-30 stocks largely kept up with the wider market gain, while electronic trading over the IBIS dealing systems were affected by interruptions caused by technical faults.

Shares in telephone giant Deutsche Telekom closed down seven pfennigs at 30.45 marks as German banks, until last Friday forbidden from publishing analysis on Telekom, gave the stock a mixed reception in their first recommendations.

The German incumbent telecom operator, floated late last year, received valuations ranging from "underweight" -- suggesting that investors should not hold too many Telekom shares in their portfolio -- through to "undervalued", implying its shares were set to rise further.
